lease protocol establishes transient ownership of weight fragments to coordinate eviction, hot - swap, and checkpoint commits without global locking. motivation and goals : - reduce cold - start token latency spikes caused by many concurrent requests touching distinct shards. - avoid large synchronous io on eviction by providing coordinated leases and soft - expiry so in - flight requests can finish using a fragment while ownership is transferred. - make hot - swap ( model binary replacement ) safer by enabling transfer of leases and graceful background rehydration of parameters. - keep runtime complexity bounded : minimal blocking paths, stateless - ish heuristics, and clear telemetries for tuning.

    "From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Authorization requested: runtime/platform staff expansion — 2 senior infra engineers

Team —

Requesting authorization to open and fill two senior infra engineer roles on the Runtime team (Platform/Serving runtime). This is a prioritized need tied to Q3 capacity and low-latency projects: KV cache improvements + compilation/kernel tuning work. Quick summary below: 

- Roles: 2 x Senior Infrastructure Engineer (runtime-focused)
- Justification: reduce token latency tail, enable sustained throughput for top 3 customers, ownership for kernel selection & quantization pipeline
- Proposed bands: Level 5 (senior) — comp band midpoint: $210k base; total comp target $260–300k depending on location/relocation
- Hiring plan: 1 hire to start immediate (SRE/infra replacement for Q3 launch), 2nd to follow after ramp of first (60–90 days) unless we get an exceptional finalist now
- Estimated run-rate impact: ~$140k–$180k incremental annual OTE per hire once fully loaded with benefits & equipment

Attached: comp-band-proposal-Q3.pdf (breakdown by region), req-brief-senior-infra-engineer.docx, and a candidate profile we want to expedite (Priya Shah).

Asks: executive authorization to convert the headcount (2 FTE) from hiring reserve and permission to extend offer to Priya (external candidate) if internal approvals clear. Please reply with any objections or sign-off.

If helpful, I can paste the mutual action plan and offer framework inline.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Runtime Platform
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: comp-band-proposal-Q3.pdf]
[Attachment: req-brief-senior-infra-engineer.docx]
[Attachment: candidate-profile-priya-shah.pdf]",
    "From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Authorization requested: runtime/platform staff expansion — 2 senior infra engineers

Vanessa —

Thanks for the packet. A couple quick clarifying items before I can greenlight: 

1) Are these in-headcount additions (new FTEs) or replacements that we shift from another team? I ask because finance needs to know if we reallocate or increase the overall team budget.
2) The comp band numbers look reasonable but please confirm the fully-loaded per-headcost you used (benefits, equity run-rate, hiring/relocation). The note you sent lists midpoint but not the 1.25x burden we normally model.
3) For the immediate candidate (Priya) — is she in the target total comp range or do we anticipate a market premium? If premium, what's the justification relative to time-to-fill risk?

If you can drop a version with the per-head fully-loaded number I can loop in finance and expedite. Otherwise I support the ask in principle.

- Marcus
VP, Infrastructure

On Thu, Jul 15, 2027 at 09:12 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> Requesting authorization... [message truncated]",
    "From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2027 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Authorization requested: runtime/platform staff expansion — 2 senior infra engineers

All —

I reviewed the proposal and the candidate profile. I can approve headcount addition in principle, pending finance confirmation on the fully loaded numbers Marcus requested. A few operational notes: 

- Please prepare an updated req brief that includes the expected ramp timeline and milestones (30/60/90). We need milestones to attach to the approval ticket.
- If Priya needs an expedited offer, recruiting should present a market comparison (3 comps) and proposed sign-on structure (if any).
- If the per-head fully-loaded exceeds $210k base midpoint by >15%, we should consider converting one hire to a contractor-to-hire with a 90-day evaluation window to reduce risk.

Mina — can you run the comps and confirm internal band alignment?

I'll hold the approval pending the items above but no fundamental objections.

— Laura
Head of People Operations
Redwood Inference

    "title": "PRD: Convert incident heatmap and operator runbook actions into staged delivery gates, synthetic checks, and rollback thresholds",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/linear",
    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"PM-991001\",\n  \"team\": \"product-management\",\n  \"title\": \"PRD: Convert incident heatmap and operator runbook actions into staged delivery gates, synthetic checks, and rollback thresholds\",\n  \"status\": \"Planned\",\n  \"priority\": \"P1\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-03-01\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-03-10\",\n  \"creator\": \"Aisha Patel\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Marcus Liu\",\n  \"project\": \"runtime-resilience-2026\",\n  \"cycle\": \"2026-W10\",\n  \"estimate\": \"5\",\n  \"due_date\": \"2026-04-15\",\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"postmortem-driven\",\n    \"slo\",\n    \"prd-gating\",\n    \"kvcache\",\n    \"runbook\"\n  ],\n  \"dependencies\": [\n    \"ENG-22178\",\n    \"PM-34012\"\n  ],\n  \"customer_impact\": \"high\",\n  \"release\": \"runtime-1.24\",\n  \"security_review_required\": \"false\",\n  \"description\": \"Background: A recent regional KV-cache incident (see linked postmortem) surfaced a set of operator runbook steps and mitigation actions that we now need to bake directly into the product requirements so future rollouts and model/kernel changes carry measurable, executable safety checks. Goal: produce a PRD update that maps postmortem action items into three concrete engineering deliverables: staged delivery gates with pass/fail criteria, synthetic and canary checks that run automatically at rollout and on demand, and clear rollback/trip thresholds tied to SLO degradation. The PRD should give engineering the acceptance criteria and observability hooks required for implementation and verification by QA and SRE teams.\",\n  \"scope\": \"In-scope: PRD text, acceptance tests, synthetic check definitions, rollout gate thresholds, runbook-triggered automated verification, links to dashboards and alert rules. Out-of-scope: actual runtime kernel changes, provisioning of extra GPUs for warm pool (these are separate ENG tickets), and customer-facing status messaging templates (handled by comms).\",\n  \"assumptions\": [\n    \"We have an existing incident postmortem with action items assigned to engineering and SRE\",\n    \"SRE owns synthetic runner and alerting infra; PM owns acceptance criteria and verification matrix\",\n    \"Rollouts will use current canary/circuit-breaker plumbing in runtime-1.24\"\n  ],\n  \"acceptance_criteria\": [\n    \"A structured PRD section exists that lists each postmortem action item and the exact delivery gate that enforces it (gate name, metric, pass/fail threshold, measurement window)\",\n    \"For every gate, there is at least one synthetic test that can be executed in CI and on-demand in staging (test definition, expected output, failure mode)\",\n    \"Rollout policy includes automated rollback triggers that map to SLO tiers: e.g., if 99th-tail latency increases by >40% over baseline for 5m across canary traffic, rollout halts and reverts\",\n    \"Observable metrics and dashboards are referenced by ID and contain token-level breakdown and tail-latency histograms required by the gate\",\n    \"QA checklist and a small suite of reproducible traffic scenarios (prefix-heavy KV-cache regen, burst cold starts, large-embedding rerun) are attached to the PRD\",\n    \"Owners and on-call contacts for gate failures are specified and aligned with runbook steps in the incident postmortem\"\n  ],\n  \"deliverables\": [\n    \"PRD section: 'Incident-derived gates and synthetic checks' (documented and reviewed)\",\n    \"Acceptance test matrix (spreadsheet) with links to synthetic runners and data sets\",\n    \"Template rollout policy with parametric thresholds (can be consumed by rollout orchestrator)\",\n    \"Verification plan for release engineering and SRE signoff\"\n  ],\n  \"outcomes\": [\n    \"Reduced time-to-detect regressions during model/kernel rollouts\",\n    \"Automated halt-and-rollback behavior for critical SLO regressions\",\n    \"Clear product requirements that reduce ambiguity for engineering and SRE implementation\"\n  ],\n  \"updates\": [\n    \"2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with SRE, Runtime, and QA to align on postmortem items to be encoded. Action: PM to map top-7 action items into candidate gates (Aisha).\",\n    \"2026-03-04: Runtime engineering clarified that prefix/KV-cache stall is measurable via existing kv_cache_regen_latency and cache_miss_ratio metrics. Added as primary gate signals.\",\n    \"2026-03-06: Decided to use two measurement windows: 5m short-term for rapid rollback triggers and 1h for degraded-state alerts. Drafted threshold proposals attached.\",\n    \"2026-03-08: SRE requested that synthetic checks include deterministic replay traffic (stored seed + prompt set). PM to add examples and storage location to PRD.\",\n    \"2026-03-10: Product review scheduled 2026-03-15. Blocker: need a dashboard link with token-level tail-latency histograms; ENG assigned ENG-22178 to add visualization.\"\n  ],\n  \"risks\": [\n    \"False positives from synthetic checks can unnecessarily block rollouts \\u2014 requires careful calibration and a muted initial rollout window\",\n    \"Insufficient historical baselines may make percentage thresholds noisy for low-volume models on Dedicated capacity\",\n    \"Ownership ambiguity between Runtime and SRE for synthetic runner maintenance could delay verification\"\n  ],\n  \"mitigations\": [\n    \"Phase 1: conservative thresholds with manual gating for first two releases; Phase 2: automated enforcement after calibration\",\n    \"Require minimum data volume before applying percentage-based thresholds; fallback to absolute-value thresholds when volume below threshold\",\n    \"Add explicit owner rows in PRD and update team runbooks to clarify synthetic runner ownership\"\n  ],\n  \"links\": [\n    \"Postmortem: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/2026-02-18-kvcache-regional-stall\",\n    \"Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd-token-latency/kvcache-heatmap\",\n    \"SRE synthetic runner: https://gitlab.redwood.ai/sre/synthetic-runner\",\n    \"PRD draft: https://docs.redwood.ai/prd/runtime-incident-gates-draft\",\n    \"Related ENG ticket: https://linear.redwood.ai/ENG-22178\"\n  ],\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Daniel Ortega\",\n    \"Priya Menon\",\n    \"Seth Ramirez (SRE)\"\n  ],\n  \"next_steps\": [\n    \"Complete first PRD draft (Aisha) by 2026-03-14\",\n    \"SRE to provision deterministic replay dataset and store path by 2026-03-12 (Seth)\",\n    \"Run a mock canary with synthetic checks in staging and record results (QA) before 2026-03-20\",\n    \"Schedule cross-team signoff meeting to approve thresholds and verification plan: target 2026-03-15\"\n  ],\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"scope\",\n    \"assumptions\",\n    \"acceptance_criteria\",\n    \"deliverables\",\n    \"outcomes\",\n    \"updates\",\n    \"risks\",\n    \"mitigations\",\n    \"next_steps\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_3dd03381e8d045d2bafa91528f6f6da3\"\n}",

document.title: PRD: Convert incident heatmap and operator runbook actions into staged delivery gates, synthetic checks, and rollback thresholds
document.content:
{
  "key": "PM-991001",
  "team": "product-management",
  "title": "PRD: Convert incident heatmap and operator runbook actions into staged delivery gates, synthetic checks, and rollback thresholds",
  "status": "Planned",
  "priority": "P1",
  "created_at": "2026-03-01",
  "updated_at": "2026-03-10",
  "creator": "Aisha Patel",
  "assignee": "Marcus Liu",
  "project": "runtime-resilience-2026",
  "cycle": "2026-W10",
  "estimate": "5",
  "due_date": "2026-04-15",
  "labels": [
    "postmortem-driven",
    "slo",
    "prd-gating",
    "kvcache",
    "runbook"
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    "ENG-22178",
    "PM-34012"
  ],
  "customer_impact": "high",
  "release": "runtime-1.24",
  "security_review_required": "false",
  "description": "Background: A recent regional KV-cache incident (see linked postmortem) surfaced a set of operator runbook steps and mitigation actions that we now need to bake directly into the product requirements so future rollouts and model/kernel changes carry measurable, executable safety checks. Goal: produce a PRD update that maps postmortem action items into three concrete engineering deliverables: staged delivery gates with pass/fail criteria, synthetic and canary checks that run automatically at rollout and on demand, and clear rollback/trip thresholds tied to SLO degradation. The PRD should give engineering the acceptance criteria and observability hooks required for implementation and verification by QA and SRE teams.",
  "scope": "In-scope: PRD text, acceptance tests, synthetic check definitions, rollout gate thresholds, runbook-triggered automated verification, links to dashboards and alert rules. Out-of-scope: actual runtime kernel changes, provisioning of extra GPUs for warm pool (these are separate ENG tickets), and customer-facing status messaging templates (handled by comms).",
  "assumptions": [
    "We have an existing incident postmortem with action items assigned to engineering and SRE",
    "SRE owns synthetic runner and alerting infra; PM owns acceptance criteria and verification matrix",
    "Rollouts will use current canary/circuit-breaker plumbing in runtime-1.24"
  ],
  "acceptance_criteria": [
    "A structured PRD section exists that lists each postmortem action item and the exact delivery gate that enforces it (gate name, metric, pass/fail threshold, measurement window)",
    "For every gate, there is at least one synthetic test that can be executed in CI and on-demand in staging (test definition, expected output, failure mode)",
    "Rollout policy includes automated rollback triggers that map to SLO tiers: e.g., if 99th-tail latency increases by >40% over baseline for 5m across canary traffic, rollout halts and reverts",
    "Observable metrics and dashboards are referenced by ID and contain token-level breakdown and tail-latency histograms required by the gate",
    "QA checklist and a small suite of reproducible traffic scenarios (prefix-heavy KV-cache regen, burst cold starts, large-embedding rerun) are attached to the PRD",
    "Owners and on-call contacts for gate failures are specified and aligned with runbook steps in the incident postmortem"
  ],
  "deliverables": [
    "PRD section: 'Incident-derived gates and synthetic checks' (documented and reviewed)",
    "Acceptance test matrix (spreadsheet) with links to synthetic runners and data sets",
    "Template rollout policy with parametric thresholds (can be consumed by rollout orchestrator)",
    "Verification plan for release engineering and SRE signoff"
  ],
  "outcomes": [
    "Reduced time-to-detect regressions during model/kernel rollouts",
    "Automated halt-and-rollback behavior for critical SLO regressions",
    "Clear product requirements that reduce ambiguity for engineering and SRE implementation"
  ],
  "updates": [
    "2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with SRE, Runtime, and QA to align on postmortem items to be encoded. Action: PM to map top-7 action items into candidate gates (Aisha).",
    "2026-03-04: Runtime engineering clarified that prefix/KV-cache stall is measurable via existing kv_cache_regen_latency and cache_miss_ratio metrics. Added as primary gate signals.",
    "2026-03-06: Decided to use two measurement windows: 5m short-term for rapid rollback triggers and 1h for degraded-state alerts. Drafted threshold proposals attached.",
    "2026-03-08: SRE requested that synthetic checks include deterministic replay traffic (stored seed + prompt set). PM to add examples and storage location to PRD.",
    "2026-03-10: Product review scheduled 2026-03-15. Blocker: need a dashboard link with token-level tail-latency histograms; ENG assigned ENG-22178 to add visualization."
  ],
  "risks": [
    "False positives from synthetic checks can unnecessarily block rollouts \u2014 requires careful calibration and a muted initial rollout window",
    "Insufficient historical baselines may make percentage thresholds noisy for low-volume models on Dedicated capacity",
    "Ownership ambiguity between Runtime and SRE for synthetic runner maintenance could delay verification"
  ],
  "mitigations": [
    "Phase 1: conservative thresholds with manual gating for first two releases; Phase 2: automated enforcement after calibration",
    "Require minimum data volume before applying percentage-based thresholds; fallback to absolute-value thresholds when volume below threshold",
    "Add explicit owner rows in PRD and update team runbooks to clarify synthetic runner ownership"
  ],
  "links": [
    "Postmortem: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/2026-02-18-kvcache-regional-stall",
    "Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd-token-latency/kvcache-heatmap",
    "SRE synthetic runner: https://gitlab.redwood.ai/sre/synthetic-runner",
    "PRD draft: https://docs.redwood.ai/prd/runtime-incident-gates-draft",
    "Related ENG ticket: https://linear.redwood.ai/ENG-22178"
  ],
  "reviewers": [
    "Daniel Ortega",
    "Priya Menon",
    "Seth Ramirez (SRE)"
  ],
  "next_steps": [
    "Complete first PRD draft (Aisha) by 2026-03-14",
    "SRE to provision deterministic replay dataset and store path by 2026-03-12 (Seth)",
    "Run a mock canary with synthetic checks in staging and record results (QA) before 2026-03-20",
    "Schedule cross-team signoff meeting to approve thresholds and verification plan: target 2026-03-15"
  ],

    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"ENG-16231\",\n  \"team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"title\": \"SLO-driven disaster recovery drill orchestration and snapshot-restore validation playbook\",\n  \"status\": \"In Progress\",\n  \"priority\": \"P0\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2025-11-10\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2025-11-19\",\n  \"creator\": \"Aisha Patel\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Diego Martinez\",\n  \"project\": \"Reliability: DR & SLOs\",\n  \"cycle\": \"2025-W46\",\n  \"estimate\": \"8\",\n  \"due_date\": \"2025-11-25\",\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"drill\",\n    \"disaster-recovery\",\n    \"SLOs\",\n    \"runbook\",\n    \"observability\",\n    \"load-shedding\",\n    \"circuit-breakers\"\n  ],\n  \"parent_issue\": [\n    \"ENG-12540\",\n    \"ENG-9487\"\n  ],\n  \"dependencies\": [\n    \"ENG-15890\",\n    \"ENG-15912\"\n  ],\n  \"customer_impact\": \"high\",\n  \"release\": \"platform-2025.11\",\n  \"security_review_required\": \"true\",\n  \"description\": \"Create a reproducible, SLO-aware active->passive failover drill runbook and automated snapshot-restore validation suite. This ticket covers: runbook authoring, orchestration tooling for scheduled drills, scripted backup verification, traffic cutover and rollback steps, circuit breaker and load-shedding validation, observable success/failure criteria tied to SLOs, and post-drill postmortem templates. Goal: prove that critical inference paths can be restored and failover completed within RTO=5m and RPO<=15m in the majority (>95%) of scheduled drills, and produce a remediation plan for recurrent failures.\",\n  \"acceptance_criteria\": [\n    \"Runbook versioned and committed in Confluence + repo (runbook v1.0)\",\n    \"Automated drill orchestration that can be scheduled and run from CI with a single command\",\n    \"Snapshot restore verification scripts that validate data integrity and KV-cache warmup within defined thresholds\",\n    \"Circuit breaker and load-shedding policies exercised and proven to keep tail latency under SLO during simulated overload\",\n    \"Successful end-to-end dry run with RTO <= 5 minutes observed and documented; issues logged if not met\",\n    \"Post-drill postmortem template filled and follow-ups scheduled for any failure modes\"\n  ],\n  \"steps\": [\n    \"Pre-drill: validate latest backups exist and pass checksum; ensure snapshots are >3 copies in different AZs/regions\",\n    \"Pre-drill: confirm canary traffic routing plan and health-check endpoints; create a temporary canary token with limited scope\",\n    \"Pre-drill: freeze non-essential deployments and schedule maintenance windows with stakeholders\",\n    \"Kick-off: trigger orchestration job that creates a fresh passive recovery cluster (in secondary region) from latest snapshots\",\n    \"Data-restore: run automated restore scripts, validate table counts, kv-store keys, and model artifact checksums\",\n    \"KV cache warmup: replay a curated prefix set to pre-warm caches; measure cold-to-warm latency profile\",\n    \"Traffic cutover: shift 1% canary traffic using traffic-router, validate traces and latency, then step to 10%, 50%, 100% following SLO gates\",\n    \"Circuit breakers: induce controlled backend overload (throttled) and verify CBs open and shed load according to policy; confirm graceful degradation responses\",\n    \"Load shedding: apply priority-based load-shedding rules and observe failure rates for low-priority requests remain within tolerance\",\n    \"Rollback: on SLO gate failure, execute scripted rollback to primary with clear rollback checklist\",\n    \"Post-drill: capture metrics, traces, and synthetic prompt evaluation scripts for quality regression checks\",\n    \"Postmortem: fill template, assign action items, and schedule remediation sprints for systemic issues\"\n  ],\n  \"observability_checks\": [\n    \"SLO dashboard: 99th/95th/50th latency, error rate, availability for inference endpoints\",\n    \"Traffic-router health and per-region capacity metrics\",\n    \"Restore validation dashboard: snapshot size, restore time, checksum pass/fail\",\n    \"KV cache hit-rate and warmup latency curves\",\n    \"Circuit breaker metrics: open/close counts, fallback counts\",\n    \"Load-shedding counters: requests dropped by policy and per-priority QoS metrics\",\n    \"Synthetic evals: prompt suites with golden responses and quality score deltas\"\n  ],\n  \"test_results_summary\": \"Dry run 2025-11-13: automated restore completed in 4m12s (within RTO), KV cache warmup reached 85% hit-rate after 6 minutes (slower than target), canary traffic cutover succeeded to 10% but failed SLO at 50% due to backend queuing under heavy burst. Root cause: kernel scheduling on dedicated GPUs delayed small-batch requests under cold start. Action items created to tune batcher thresholds and add pre-warm hooks.\",\n  \"comments\": [\n    \"2025-11-10 Aisha Patel: Ticket created after reliability review; priority set to P0. Initial scope includes orchestration, restore validation, and CB/load-shed exercises.\",\n    \"2025-11-11 Diego Martinez: Proposed orchestration approach uses existing CI pipeline + 'drill-runner' Lambda to spawn recovery infra; shared draft runbook in Confluence: https://confluence.internal/redwood/drill-runbook-draft\",\n    \"2025-11-12 Sofia Nguyen (Eng-Infra): Added scripts to repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/drill-scripts/pull/211; need infra approval for secondary-region quotas\",\n    \"2025-11-13 Dry run executed by Diego Martinez and Sofia Nguyen; initial pass but observed cache warmup slowness and backend kernel prioritization issue. Logs and traces uploaded: https://dashboards.internal/redwood/drills/ENG-16231/2025-11-13\",\n    \"2025-11-15 Design review: agreed to add explicit 'warmup' stage and expand synthetic prompt suite to cover tail-case prompts (edge-case sequences).\",\n    \"2025-11-17 Ops: raised quota request with cloud provider for secondary region (ticket CLOUD-4328).\",\n    \"2025-11-18 Diego Martinez: Updated runbook to include clear rollback checklist and SLA gates; scheduled next drill 2025-11-24\",\n    \"2025-11-19 Aisha Patel: Marking next steps: tune batcher kernel selection, add automated alert if KV-cache hit-rate < 70% after 5m, and get security review for drill orchestration IAM roles.\"\n  ],\n  \"notes\": [\n    \"Confluence runbook draft: https://confluence.internal/redwood/drill-runbook-draft\",\n    \"GitHub orchestration PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/drill-scripts/pull/211\",\n    \"Restore validation scripts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/restore-verifier\",\n    \"SLO dashboard (editable): https://dashboards.internal/redwood/slo/drill-overview\",\n    \"Incident learning reference: ENG-9487 inventory & failover playbook\",\n    \"Customer-facing comms template: https://docs.google.com/document/d/DRILL-comm-template\"\n  ],\n  \"runbook_version\": \"v0.9\",\n  \"communication_plan\": [\n    \"3 days before: email notice to SRE/Platform/Support/PMs with drill window and blast radius\",\n    \"1 hour before: Slack #ops-alert pinned message and incident channel created\",\n    \"During drill: automated progress updates to channel from drill-runner (canary %, restore time)\",\n    \"Post-drill: 1-hour readout with metrics and initial findings; full postmortem within 72 hours\"\n  ],\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"acceptance_criteria\",\n    \"steps\",\n    \"observability_checks\",\n    \"test_results_summary\",\n    \"comments\",\n    \"notes\",\n    \"communication_plan\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_cfe3fb2db8bd446286e74dfbb2db0ef7\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: SLO-driven disaster recovery drill orchestration and snapshot-restore validation playbook\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-16231-slo-driven-drill-orchestration-restore-playbook.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: engineering\nProject: Reliability: DR & SLOs\nTeam: engineering\n\n- pre - drill : validate latest backups exist and pass checksum ; ensure snapshots are > 3 copies in different azs / regions - pre - drill : confirm canary traffic routing plan and health - check endpoints ; create a temporary canary token with limited scope - pre - drill : freeze non - essential deployments and schedule maintenance windows with stakeholders - kick - off : trigger orchestration job that creates a fresh passive recovery cluster ( in secondary region ) from latest snapshots - data - restore : run automated restore scripts, validate table counts, kv - store keys, and model artifact checksums - kv cache warmup : replay a curated prefix set to pre - warm caches ; measure cold - to - warm latency profile - traffic cutover : shift 1 %",

{
  "document": {
    "id": "dsid_94def0ce27f34496989dbd82ae7fd912",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/team-wiki/cross-layer-diagnostics-and-observability-playbook-2026.json",
    "title": "Cross-layer Observability & Diagnostics Playbook — Burst and Degradation Incidents",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Cross-layer Observability & Diagnostics Playbook \\u2014 Burst and Degradation Incidents\",\n  \"space\": \"eng-serving-runtime\",\n  \"author\": \"Aisha Kapoor\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2025-11-12\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2026-03-01\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Marco Ruiz\",\n    \"Evelyn Park\",\n    \"Daniel Kim\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"observability\",\n    \"runbook\",\n    \"profiling\",\n    \"benchmarking\",\n    \"kernel-scheduling\",\n    \"incident-response\"\n  ],\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/runtime-deployment-circuit-breakers-and-sla-fallback-playbook-2026\",\n    \"confluence/eng-serving-runtime/profiling-playbook/telemetry-feedback-kernel-autotune-playbook-2026\",\n    \"confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite/mixed-workload-slo-simulation-suite-2026\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"internal\",\n  \"content\": \"Summary\\n-------\\nThis playbook describes a cross-layer, repeatable approach for detecting, diagnosing, and mitigating short-duration bursts and progressive degradation in the Serving Runtime. It bridges runtime architecture, kernel scheduling signals, profiling playbooks, and benchmarking checks so oncall and runtime engineers can quickly restore SLOs and reduce mean time to innocence (MTTI).\\n\\nScope and audience\\n------------------\\n- Scope: Hosted + Dedicated runtime clusters and the operator-facing control-plane paths (Dispatcher, SlotAllocator, KernelRunner, KVCache, and Runtime Router).\\n- Audience: Serving runtime oncall, runtime engineers, release owners, and performance SREs.\\n\\nGoals and SLO references\\n------------------------\\n- Primary detection SLOs: 95th token-latency < 100ms, 99th token-latency < 300ms for default small-model profile. (See per-model SLO sheet.)\\n- Operational goals: initial triage within 5 minutes, mitigation (fallback or ramp) within 15 minutes, restore to within 10% of baseline P95 within 60 minutes.\\n\\nHow this playbook fits with other docs\\n-------------------------------------\\nThis is an operational layer that references: profiling playbooks for telemetry sampling, kernel-scheduler design docs for decision points, benchmarking suite for reproducible load, and existing runbooks for fallback and warmstart. Use this playbook when alerts indicate sudden tail-latency or progressive throughput drop.\\n\\nKey concepts and system components\\n----------------------------------\\n- Dispatcher: user-facing ingress that performs request classification and route affinity. Primary source of request-level traces.\\n- SlotAllocator: assigns execution slots (cohort/priority) used by the scheduler. Tracks queue lengths and admission metrics.\\n- KernelRunner: GPU process pool executing kernels. Emits kernel_latency_hist, kernel_qps, kernel_error_rate, and kernel_memory_pressure.\\n- KVCache: per-session prefix cache. Key signals: hit_rate, eviction_rate, and warmup_latency.\\n- Runtime Router / Graceful Fallback: orchestrates model variant fallbacks and cross-region routing.\\n\\nSignal catalog and quick thresholds\\n----------------------------------\\n(Use these to prioritize initial checks.)\\n\\n| Signal (metric)                      | Type         | Quick threshold (when to escalate) |\\n|--------------------------------------|--------------|------------------------------------|\\n| dispatch.request_p95_ms              | latency      | > baseline * 1.2 or > 200ms       |\\n| kernel_latency_p95_ms                | latency      | > 1.5x baseline                   |\\n| kernel_queue_depth                   | gauge        | > 80% of max slots                |\\n| slot_allocator.queue_wait_time_p95   | latency      | > 50ms                            |\\n| kvcache.hit_rate                     | ratio        | drop > 15 percentage points       |\\n| grpc.reconnect_rate                  | rate         | sustained > 5/min                 |\\n| node_gpu_utilization                 | utilization  | > 95% (thermal risk)              |\\n| infra.network_rtt_p95                | latency      | > baseline + 20ms                 |\\n\\nNote: baseline is the rolling 7-day median for the service and model profile.\\n\\nTriage checklist (first 5 minutes)\\n----------------------------------\\n1) Validate alert and scope\\n   - Confirm alert: check Alerting UI + trace sample in the last 2 minutes.\\n   - Determine scope: single node, single pool, entire region, or global. Use the Dispatcher topology view.\\n2) Quick telemetry pull\\n   - Pull P95/P99 for dispatch.*, kernel_*, kvcache.* and slot_allocator.* for last 30m vs 3h.\\n   - Commands (on the runbook box):\\n     ```bash\\n     rmetric query --service=dispatcher --metrics=\\\"dispatch.request_p95_ms,dispatch.request_p99_ms\\\" --range=30m\\n     rmetric query --pool=kernerrunner --metrics=\\\"kernel_latency_p95_ms,kernel_queue_depth\\\" --range=30m\\n     rlog fetch --trace-id $(rmetric top-traces --service=dispatcher --limit=1) --follow=1m\\n     ```\\n3) Fast isolation heuristics\\n   - If kernel_queue_depth high and kernel_latency rising: likely kernel scheduling or admission.\\n   - If kvcache.hit_rate collapsed and kernel P95 is higher: consider cache warmup cascade.\\n   - If node_gpu_utilization is low but kernel queue depth is high: investigate scheduler admission/NUMA balance.\\n\\nIsolation procedures (15\\u201330 minutes)\\n-----------------------------------\\nA. Kernel scheduling checks\\n   - Check scheduler decision log: `rkctl scheduler inspect --pool <pool> --window 10m`\\n   - Look for recent policy changes (priority weights, admission caps). If there was a rollout in the last hour, rollback to the previous scheduler config.\\n   - Check GPU mismatch signals: `rkctl node inspect --node <id>` -> note nvlink errors, thermal events.\\nB. Admission and backpressure\\n   - Validate admission thresholds: `SlotAllocator.admit_rate` vs observed arrival rate.\\n   - If admission is overly conservative, temporarily increase soft-cap by +10% and monitor.\\n   - If admission is broken, flip to the safe fallback profile: `rkctl route set-fallback --route <route> --profile reduced-memory`\\nC. KV cache warmup cascade\\n   - If kvcache.eviction_rate spiked, trigger a targeted prefetch job for the affected sessions:\\n     ```yaml\\n     apiVersion: redwood.io/v1\\n     kind: KVPatchJob\\n     spec:\\n       model: <model-name>\\n       sessions: [session-ids-file]\\n       concurrency: 4\\n     ```\\n\\nMitigation patterns (approved temporary actions)\\n------------------------------------------------\\n- Short term (minutes): route to warm fallback model variant in-region; increase admission soft-cap by 5\\u201310%; reduce batch size target to lower per-call kernel time.\\n- Medium term (hours): evict peaky low-util priority cohorts; initiate rolling restart of KernelRunner pool if drivers show instability; apply kernel restart mitigation which drains pending short calls first.\\n- Long term (post-incident): schedule simulation in the benchmarking suite to reproduce the burst, add synthetic traffic signature to the mixed-workload SLO test, and create a scheduler policy change with canary and rollout plan.\\n\\nDiagnostic playbook for kernel-level regressions\\n------------------------------------------------\\n1) Reproduce with a targeted microbenchmark\\n   - Use the perf harness: `bench-run --profile kernel-latency --model <model> --sequence 256 --concurrency 8 --duration 5m`\\n   - Collect kernel traces: `kerntrace collect --pool <pool> --out /tmp/kerntrace.pb`\\n2) Compare kernel signature to baseline\\n   - Run diff against golden: `kerntrace diff /tmp/kerntrace.pb gs://benchmarks/kernel-gold/<model>.pb`\\n3) If reproducible, tag as kernel-regression and create a hotfix branch with kernel config rollback. Include the diff and perf artifacts in the PR.\\n\\nBenchmarks and quick acceptance tests\\n------------------------------------\\nUse the standard benchmarking suite to validate mitigations before full rollout. Minimum test matrix:\\n- Mixed workload replay (30m): baseline QPS, 30% long sequences, 20% high-concurrency short sequences.\\n- Kernel microbench: 1\\u20138 batch sizes, sequence 16/128/512.\\n- Admission and fallback test: inject synthetic saturating arrival and assert fallback triggers within 10s.\\n\\nSample benchmark run (CLI)\\n```bash\\nbenchctl run --suite mixed-workload --tag incident-capture-$(date +%s) --params \\\"qps=500,duration=30m,seqmix=0.3:512,0.5:128,0.2:16\\\"\\nbenchctl collect --artifact incident-capture-1234 --to gs://bench-results/incident-capture-1234\\n```\\n\\nRelease notes and change correlation\\n-----------------------------------\\n- Always check the Deployment Log (release-control) for any scheduler or kernel config changes in the 60 minutes before incident start.\\n- Use the release correlation query: `rctl releases list --since 1h --component scheduler,kernerrunner,kvcache`\\n- If a canary rollout is present, pause or rollback the canary immediately and re-evaluate.\\n\\nKnown issues to consider (fast checks)\\n------------------------------------\\n- NVLINK flapping on a subset of nodes causes intermittent kernel stalls (workaround: cordon nodes with nvlink_errors > 0 and drain after cooldown).\\n- Kernel memory fragmentation causing soft OOMs under interleaved batches (mitigation: apply compacting GC in 2.3.1-hotfix and restart KernelRunner).\\n- GRPC connection recycling leading to small head-of-line stalls at the Dispatcher (workaround: increase connection pool size temporarily).\\n\\nRunbook appendices and artifacts to collect\\n-------------------------------------------\\nCollect these during the incident and attach to the postmortem:\\n- Top 20 traces (dispatch) during incident window.\\n- kernel_trace.pb files for affected KernelRunner nodes.\\n- SlotAllocator decision log for the interval.\\n- Bench artifacts if a reproduction was run (benchctl outputs).\\n- Release correlation snapshot (release-control export).\\n\\nPost-incident actions (owner: runtime-performance squad)\\n-------------------------------------------------------\\n1) Assign postmortem owner within 24h.\\n2) Reproduce incident in bench lab with identical traffic signature within 72h.\\n3) Create follow-up tickets: scheduler policy change, kernel tuning, KVCache prefetch improvements, or infra remediation (if hardware).\\n4) Add a synthetic SLO probe to the mixed-workload suite for future detection.\\n\\nOperational contacts and escalation\\n----------------------------------\\n- Oncall (runtime): #runtime-oncall Slack, Pager schedule in PagerDuty\\n- Kernel squadra: kern-team@redwood.com\\n- Infra hardware: infra-hw@redwood.com\\n\\nMaintenance checklist (for release owners)\\n-----------------------------------------\\n- Before rolling scheduler changes: run the canary matrix (3% traffic) for 60 minutes document.title: Cross-layer Observability & Diagnostics Playbook — Burst and Degradation Incidents
document.content:
{
  "title": "Cross-layer Observability & Diagnostics Playbook — Burst and Degradation Incidents",
  "space": "eng-serving-runtime",
  "author": "Aisha Kapoor",
  "owner_team": "engineering",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2025-11-12",
  "last_updated": "2026-03-01",
  "reviewers": [
    "Marco Ruiz",
    "Evelyn Park",
    "Daniel Kim"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "observability",
    "runbook",
    "profiling",
    "benchmarking",
    "kernel-scheduling",
    "incident-response"
  ],
  "related_pages": [
    "confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/runtime-deployment-circuit-breakers-and-sla-fallback-playbook-2026",
    "confluence/eng-serving-runtime/profiling-playbook/telemetry-feedback-kernel-autotune-playbook-2026",
    "confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite/mixed-workload-slo-simulation-suite-2026"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "content": "Summary
-------
This playbook describes a cross-layer, repeatable approach for detecting, diagnosing, and mitigating short-duration bursts and progressive degradation in the Serving Runtime. It bridges runtime architecture, kernel scheduling signals, profiling playbooks, and benchmarking checks so oncall and runtime engineers can quickly restore SLOs and reduce mean time to innocence (MTTI).

Scope and audience
------------------
- Scope: Hosted + Dedicated runtime clusters and the operator-facing control-plane paths (Dispatcher, SlotAllocator, KernelRunner, KVCache, and Runtime Router).
- Audience: Serving runtime oncall, runtime engineers, release owners, and performance SREs.

Goals and SLO references
------------------------
- Primary detection SLOs: 95th token-latency < 100ms, 99th token-latency < 300ms for default small-model profile. (See per-model SLO sheet.)
- Operational goals: initial triage within 5 minutes, mitigation (fallback or ramp) within 15 minutes, restore to within 10% of baseline P95 within 60 minutes.

How this playbook fits with other docs
-------------------------------------
This is an operational layer that references: profiling playbooks for telemetry sampling, kernel-scheduler design docs for decision points, benchmarking suite for reproducible load, and existing runbooks for fallback and warmstart. Use this playbook when alerts indicate sudden tail-latency or progressive throughput drop.

Key concepts and system components
----------------------------------
- Dispatcher: user-facing ingress that performs request classification and route affinity. Primary source of request-level traces.
- SlotAllocator: assigns execution slots (cohort/priority) used by the scheduler. Tracks queue lengths and admission metrics.
- KernelRunner: GPU process pool executing kernels. Emits kernel_latency_hist, kernel_qps, kernel_error_rate, and kernel_memory_pressure.
- KVCache: per-session prefix cache. Key signals: hit_rate, eviction_rate, and warmup_latency.
- Runtime Router / Graceful Fallback: orchestrates model variant fallbacks and cross-region routing.

Signal catalog and quick thresholds
----------------------------------
(Use these to prioritize initial checks.)

| Signal (metric)                      | Type         | Quick threshold (when to escalate) |
|--------------------------------------|--------------|------------------------------------|
| dispatch.request_p95_ms              | latency      | > baseline * 1.2 or > 200ms       |
| kernel_latency_p95_ms                | latency      | > 1.5x baseline                   |
| kernel_queue_depth                   | gauge        | > 80% of max slots                |
| slot_allocator.queue_wait_time_p95   | latency      | > 50ms                            |
| kvcache.hit_rate                     | ratio        | drop > 15 percentage points       |
| grpc.reconnect_rate                  | rate         | sustained > 5/min                 |
| node_gpu_utilization                 | utilization  | > 95% (thermal risk)              |
| infra.network_rtt_p95                | latency      | > baseline + 20ms                 |

Note: baseline is the rolling 7-day median for the service and model profile.

Triage checklist (first 5 minutes)
----------------------------------
1) Validate alert and scope
   - Confirm alert: check Alerting UI + trace sample in the last 2 minutes.
   - Determine scope: single node, single pool, entire region, or global. Use the Dispatcher topology view.
2) Quick telemetry pull
   - Pull P95/P99 for dispatch.*, kernel_*, kvcache.* and slot_allocator.* for last 30m vs 3h.
   - Commands (on the runbook box):
     ```bash
     rmetric query --service=dispatcher --metrics="dispatch.request_p95_ms,dispatch.request_p99_ms" --range=30m
     rmetric query --pool=kernerrunner --metrics="kernel_latency_p95_ms,kernel_queue_depth" --range=30m
     rlog fetch --trace-id $(rmetric top-traces --service=dispatcher --limit=1) --follow=1m
     ```
3) Fast isolation heuristics
   - If kernel_queue_depth high and kernel_latency rising: likely kernel scheduling or admission.
   - If kvcache.hit_rate collapsed and kernel P95 is higher: consider cache warmup cascade.
   - If node_gpu_utilization is low but kernel queue depth is high: investigate scheduler admission/NUMA balance.

Isolation procedures (15–30 minutes)
-----------------------------------
A. Kernel scheduling checks
   - Check scheduler decision log: `rkctl scheduler inspect --pool <pool> --window 10m`
   - Look for recent policy changes (priority weights, admission caps). If there was a rollout in the last hour, rollback to the previous scheduler config.
   - Check GPU mismatch signals: `rkctl node inspect --node <id>` -> note nvlink errors, thermal events.
B. Admission and backpressure
   - Validate admission thresholds: `SlotAllocator.admit_rate` vs observed arrival rate.
   - If admission is overly conservative, temporarily increase soft-cap by +10% and monitor.
   - If admission is broken, flip to the safe fallback profile: `rkctl route set-fallback --route <route> --profile reduced-memory`
C. KV cache warmup cascade
   - If kvcache.eviction_rate spiked, trigger a targeted prefetch job for the affected sessions:
     ```yaml
     apiVersion: redwood.io/v1
     kind: KVPatchJob
     spec:
       model: <model-name>
       sessions: [session-ids-file]
       concurrency: 4
     ```

Mitigation patterns (approved temporary actions)
------------------------------------------------
- Short term (minutes): route to warm fallback model variant in-region; increase admission soft-cap by 5–10%; reduce batch size target to lower per-call kernel time.
- Medium term (hours): evict peaky low-util priority cohorts; initiate rolling restart of KernelRunner pool if drivers show instability; apply kernel restart mitigation which drains pending short calls first.
- Long term (post-incident): schedule simulation in the benchmarking suite to reproduce the burst, add synthetic traffic signature to the mixed-workload SLO test, and create a scheduler policy change with canary and rollout plan.

Diagnostic playbook for kernel-level regressions
------------------------------------------------
1) Reproduce with a targeted microbenchmark
   - Use the perf harness: `bench-run --profile kernel-latency --model <model> --sequence 256 --concurrency 8 --duration 5m`
   - Collect kernel traces: `kerntrace collect --pool <pool> --out /tmp/kerntrace.pb`
2) Compare kernel signature to baseline
   - Run diff against golden: `kerntrace diff /tmp/kerntrace.pb gs://benchmarks/kernel-gold/<model>.pb`
3) If reproducible, tag as kernel-regression and create a hotfix branch with kernel config rollback. Include the diff and perf artifacts in the PR.

Benchmarks and quick acceptance tests
------------------------------------
Use the standard benchmarking suite to validate mitigations before full rollout. Minimum test matrix:
- Mixed workload replay (30m): baseline QPS, 30% long sequences, 20% high-concurrency short sequences.
- Kernel microbench: 1–8 batch sizes, sequence 16/128/512.
- Admission and fallback test: inject synthetic saturating arrival and assert fallback triggers within 10s.

Sample benchmark run (CLI)
```bash
benchctl run --suite mixed-workload --tag incident-capture-$(date +%s) --params "qps=500,duration=30m,seqmix=0.3:512,0.5:128,0.2:16"
benchctl collect --artifact incident-capture-1234 --to gs://bench-results/incident-capture-1234
```

Release notes and change correlation
-----------------------------------
- Always check the Deployment Log (release-control) for any scheduler or kernel config changes in the 60 minutes before incident start.
- Use the release correlation query: `rctl releases list --since 1h --component scheduler,kernerrunner,kvcache`
- If a canary rollout is present, pause or rollback the canary immediately and re-evaluate.

Known issues to consider (fast checks)
------------------------------------
- NVLINK flapping on a subset of nodes causes intermittent kernel stalls (workaround: cordon nodes with nvlink_errors > 0 and drain after cooldown).
- Kernel memory fragmentation causing soft OOMs under interleaved batches (mitigation: apply compacting GC in 2.3.1-hotfix and restart KernelRunner).
- GRPC connection recycling leading to small head-of-line stalls at the Dispatcher (workaround: increase connection pool size temporarily).

Runbook appendices and artifacts to collect
-------------------------------------------
Collect these during the incident and attach to the postmortem:
- Top 20 traces (dispatch) during incident window.
- kernel_trace.pb files for affected KernelRunner nodes.
- SlotAllocator decision log for the interval.
- Bench artifacts if a reproduction was run (benchctl outputs).
- Release correlation snapshot (release-control export).

Post-incident actions (owner: runtime-performance squad)
-------------------------------------------------------
1) Assign postmortem owner within 24h.
2) Reproduce incident in bench lab with identical traffic signature within 72h.
3) Create follow-up tickets: scheduler policy change, kernel tuning, KVCache prefetch improvements, or infra remediation (if hardware).
4) Add a synthetic SLO probe to the mixed-workload suite for future detection.

Operational contacts and escalation
----------------------------------
- Oncall (runtime): #runtime-oncall Slack, Pager schedule in PagerDuty
- Kernel squadra: kern-team@redwood.com
- Infra hardware: infra-hw@redwood.com

Maintenance checklist (for release owners)
-----------------------------------------
- Before rolling scheduler changes: run the canary matrix (3% traffic) for 60 minutes against mixed workload.
- Attach bench artifacts and kernel diffs to the PR.
- Notify SRE and runtime performance reviewers 24h prior to rollout.

Revision history
----------------
- 2025-11-12: initial draft (Aisha Kapoor)
- 2026-01-18: added KVCache warmup cascade procedures and benchmark commands (reviewers: Marco Ruiz)
- 2026-03-01: expanded kernel-level diagnostics and known issues section; published (reviewers: Evelyn Park, Daniel Kim)

Related resources and links
-------------------------
- Dispatcher traces dashboard: /dashboards/dispatcher/traces
- Mixed-workload bench suite: /tools/benchctl/doc
- Scheduler policy language reference: confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/scheduler-policy-language-declarative-profiles-2026
- Kernel tracing guide: confluence/eng-serving-runtime/profiling-playbook/kernel-observability-sla-profiling-cadence-2024

If you have questions or need a walkthrough, ping the runtime-performance squad in #runtime-performance and request a live lab replication session.",
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "content"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_94def0ce27f34496989dbd82ae7fd912"
}

{
  "channel": "incidents",
  "thread_ts": "1738501234",
  "first_message_ts": "1738501234",
  "last_message_ts": "1738501899",
  "participants": [
    "incident-bot",
    "pagerduty",
    "emma_oncall",
    "sandeep_sre",
    "olivia_releases",
    "nate_platform",
    "cs_bot"
  ],
  "messages": "incident-bot: PagerDuty ALERT: service=canary-router severity=critical \u2014 error-rate > 5% for 3m, triggered at 1738501234. Pager: @emma_oncall.\npagerduty: auto-page fired -> P123456: Canary routing 503 spike (canary-router). Escalation policy: oncall -> sre -> eng.\nemma_oncall: acked P123456 :wave: I'm on it, pulling logs and checking canary metrics. Any deploy in the last 30m? @olivia_releases\nolivia_releases: deploying release/2026.03.15-canary two minutes before alert. Canary fraction 5%. Rolling out edge-proxy + router changes.\nsandeep_sre: seeing high 503s on canary-router pods, p95 latency up. Metrics: backend-conns exhausted? Dumping pod logs.\nemma_oncall: logs show repeated grpc: EOF and connection reset. Attaching sample: ```2026-03-15T03:20:12Z canary-router[abc123] ERROR connection reset by peer while proxying to model-backend-quant```\nnate_platform: checking LB metrics \u2014 upstream health for canary backends fluctuating. A few pods have OOMKill in last 2m. Node memory pressure maybe.\nolivia_releases: rollback flag? We can cut canary to 0% traffic. Rollout controller: redwoodctl rollout set canary-router --fraction=0. Runbook suggests traffic diversion first.\nemma_oncall: doing diversion now. Command: ```redwoodctl traffic split canary-router --from=0.05 --to=0.0 --timeout=30s```\nincident-bot: Command executed by @emma_oncall at 1738501335 \u2014 traffic fraction stepping to 0. Canary fraction now 0.00.\nsandeep_sre: after divert, 503 rate dropped to baseline within 40s. p95 latency back to normal. Looks like issue confined to canary variant (new router build).\nolivia_releases: confirmed canary variant has memory regression with quant kernel. Pinned to older image in CI we should revert. Will open rollback PR.\nemma_oncall: P123456 update: mitigated customer-facing error by diverting canary -> incident severity reduced to major. Notifying CS. @cs_bot please run status page draft.\ncs_bot: Draft status: \"We experienced increased errors for a subset of requests routed to a canary release. Traffic was diverted and service restored. Engineers are investigating the release and users may see intermittent 503s between 03:20-03:24 UTC.\" Would you like to post? :eyes:\nemma_oncall: Post now. Also tagging @sandeep_sre for postmortem. Add timeline + CI diff.\nsandeep_sre: collecting diagnostics \u2014 attaching heap profiles and kernel logs. Noted OOM lines correlate with the quant kernel change in release/2026.03.15-canary. Will correlate memory usage from 03:15-03:25.\nolivia_releases: opened rollback PR #342: revert router kernel patch. Will coordinate with eng to validate a canaryless rollback to stable image and then re-run canary with memory guardrails.\npagerduty: P123456 status -> acknowledged by @emma_oncall at 1738501250, mitigated at 1738501360, resolved at 1738501899 by @olivia_releases (post-rollout rollback merged).\nemma_oncall: handoff summary for follow-up: root cause likely memory regression in quant kernel within router image \u2014 triggered OOMs in canary and exposed by spike. Mitigation: immediate traffic diversion, rollback PR merged, monitor for recurrence. Next steps: full postmortem with CI diff, add memory safety tests, add alert for canary pod OOMs.\nolivia_releases: thanks team. I'll schedule the rollback verification run and coordinate a staged re-rollout after fixes. Marking the incident as resolved in PD and closing thread. :white_check_mark:\nincident-bot: Incident P123456 marked resolved by @olivia_releases at 1738501899. Summary logged to incidents repo: /incidents/2026-03-15-canary-quant-memory-regression.md\"",

  "content_field_names": [
    "messages"
  ],

}

    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/google_drive",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Preemption fairness regression and eviction wave diagnostics\",\n  \"owner\": \"Priya Shah\",\n  \"drive_area\": \"shared_drives\",\n  \"path\": \"shared_drives/engineering/site-reliability-engineering/preemption-fairness-regression-and-eviction-wave-diagnostics.json\",\n  \"doc_type\": \"doc\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-02-10\",\n  \"last_modified\": \"2026-02-14\",\n  \"collaborators\": [\n    \"Ethan Morales\",\n    \"Claire Zhang\",\n    \"Luis Ortega\"\n  ],\n  \"team\": \"eng-sre\",\n  \"status\": \"in_review\",\n  \"tags\": [\n    \"scheduler\",\n    \"preemption\",\n    \"eviction\",\n    \"kubernetes\",\n    \"triage\",\n    \"us-west-2\"\n  ],\n  \"linked_artifacts\": [\n    \"https://linear.app/RED-1934\",\n    \"https://github.com/redwood-inference/k8s-scheduler/commit/4f3a9b\",\n    \"https://grafana.redwood.com/d/cluster/scheduler-metrics?var-region=us-west-2\"\n  ],\n  \"summary\": \"Notes from initial on-call triage for a sudden cluster-wide spike in pod preemptions and correlated eviction waves in us-west-2. Suspected regression introduced by scheduler scoring plugin change deployed in the 2026-02-09 rollout. This doc captures observations, commands we ran, mitigation we applied, and proposed follow-ups.\",\n  \"symptoms\": \"Between 03:15 and 03:40 UTC, multiple namespaces reported large numbers of Pending -> Evicted/Preempted events. Pod restart churn increased, user-reported 503s from inference endpoints, autoscaler oscillations triggered by rapid pod churn. Node available resources (Allocatable CPU/memory) did not show cluster-level shortage \\u2014 rather, pods were being preempted out of nodes where they previously ran for days. Scheduler logs show increased Preemption decisions and score ties.\",\n  \"quick_timeline\": \"2026-02-09 22:30 PST: rolling deploy of scheduler v1.27-custom with new scoring plugin (strict-topology) to control bin-packing\\n2026-02-10 03:17 UTC: Pager triggered for increased pod restarts in us-west-2 prod cluster\\n03:20 UTC: SRE oncall (Priya) starts triage, confirms spike in Preemption events via kubectl and Grafana\\n03:28 UTC: Rolled back scheduler to previous version in control-plane for us-west-2 (partial)\\n03:40 UTC: Preemption rate drops, evictions stabilize; follow-up investigation started\",\n  \"metrics_observed\": \"Preemption rate: baseline ~0.05/hr -> spike peaking at ~32/hr across AZs;\\nScheduler internal latency 99th: 120ms -> 650ms during spike;\\nEviction count (pods): +560 in 30 minutes in production;\\nNode pressure metrics (cpu/mem): no cluster-wide shortage, per-node CPU usage unchanged;\\nPod startup time median: 2.1s -> 8.9s because of restart churn\",\n  \"commands_run\": \"kubectl get events --all-namespaces --field-selector reason=Preempted -o wide | head -n 200\\nkubectl describe node ip-10-0-4-23 | egrep -A4 'Non-terminated Pods'\\njournalctl -u kube-scheduler -o cat | sed -n '1,200p' | grep -i preempt\\nkubectl get pods -n prod -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,PRIORITY:.spec.priority,STATUS:.status.phase --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp | tail -n 100\\ncurl -sS \\\"https://grafana.redwood.com/render/d-solo/cluster/scheduler-metrics?panelId=3&from=now-1h&to=now\\\" -o scheduler-preemption.png\",\n  \"root_cause_hypotheses\": \"1) Scoring plugin change introduced different tie-breaking behavior that aggressively favors preempting medium-priority pods when topology-scores are tied.\\n2) A scheduling race under load increased scheduler latency causing stale scheduling decisions and duplicate preemption candidates.\\n3) Mistuned preemption cost heuristics in our custom scheduler fork (recent commit 4f3a9b) increased preemption score delta for low-memory nodes.\\nEvidence: timing correlates with scheduler rollout; logs show many preemption decisions with identical scores; rollback reduced rate.\",\n  \"mitigation_steps_taken\": \"1) Immediate rollback of scheduler binary in us-west-2 control plane partial rollout (~03:28 UTC).\\n2) Temporarily increased eviction gracePeriod for critical namespaces to reduce restart churn (patch applied to pod disruption budgets).\\n3) Added a temporary admission webhook block for best-effort pods in prod to avoid low-priority churn while we investigate.\\nOutcome: preemption rate dropped to baseline within ~12 minutes of rollback; user-facing errors decreased.\",\n  \"persistent_actions\": \"- Create a canary rollout plan for scheduler scoring plugin updates with traffic shaping and synthetic preemption checks.\\n- Add unit/integration test that simulates score ties and verifies deterministic tie-breaking consistent with prior behavior.\\n- Audit custom preemption heuristics in commit history and add guardrails (feature flag + kill switch).\\n- Add Grafana alert to detect preemption rate > 5/hr sustained for 5 minutes per region.\",\n  \"next_steps\": \"- Full postmortem to be written after deeper log correlation and scheduler trace capture (owner: Priya, due 2026-02-18).\\n- Reproduce locally: create a mini-cluster with our custom scheduler and run the synthetic workload that caused tie scores. (Ethan)\\n- Patch scheduler to preserve previous tie-break ordering or make tie-break explicit, then perform staged rollout with 1% canary. (Claire)\\n- Follow up with product teams about autoscaler backoff behavior to reduce oscillation during similar events.\",\n  \"notes_to_oncall\": \"If you see a preemption spike: 1) check scheduler rollout history (kubectl -n kube-system rollout history deployment/kube-scheduler); 2) query recent scheduler logs for 'Preemption' and 'score tie' strings; 3) consider partial rollback of scheduler binary if correlating with deploy; 4) temporarily raise critical pod terminationGracePeriod and pause non-essential jobs; 5) ping eng-sre Slack #sre-oncall and cc @Priya and @Ethan. Include timestamps and sample pod names when filing a follow-up Linear ticket.\",\n  \"freeform_notes\": \"- Observed interesting pattern: many preempted pods shared same topologySpread constraints; scoring plugin was aggressively trying to satisfy topologies which produced more preemption candidates than before.\\n- Autoscaler amplified problem: nodes freed by preemptions triggered scale-down observations in ASG, which then forced additional re-scheduling and further churn.\\n- Consider adding a short cooldown on node-scale-down when preemption rate is high.\\n- Need to coordinate rollback/playbook with Platform team to avoid control-plane config drift in future deploys.\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"summary\",\n    \"symptoms\",\n    \"quick_timeline\",\n    \"metrics_observed\",\n    \"commands_run\",\n    \"root_cause_hypotheses\",\n    \"mitigation_steps_taken\",\n    \"persistent_actions\",\n    \"next_steps\",\n    \"notes_to_oncall\",\n    \"freeform_notes\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_62b9695b49a446acaa1f59a1427b8480\"\n}",

{
  "title": "Preemption fairness regression and eviction wave diagnostics",
  "owner": "Priya Shah",
  "drive_area": "shared_drives",
  "path": "shared_drives/engineering/site-reliability-engineering/preemption-fairness-regression-and-eviction-wave-diagnostics.json",
  "doc_type": "doc",
  "created_at": "2026-02-10",
  "last_modified": "2026-02-14",
  "collaborators": [
    "Ethan Morales",
    "Claire Zhang",
    "Luis Ortega"
  ],
  "team": "eng-sre",
  "status": "in_review",
  "tags": [
    "scheduler",
    "preemption",
    "eviction",
    "kubernetes",
    "triage",
    "us-west-2"
  ],
  "linked_artifacts": [
    "https://linear.app/RED-1934",
    "https://github.com/redwood-inference/k8s-scheduler/commit/4f3a9b",
    "https://grafana.redwood.com/d/cluster/scheduler-metrics?var-region=us-west-2"
  ],
  "summary": "Notes from initial on-call triage for a sudden cluster-wide spike in pod preemptions and correlated eviction waves in us-west-2. Suspected regression introduced by scheduler scoring plugin change deployed in the 2026-02-09 rollout. This doc captures observations, commands we ran, mitigation we applied, and proposed follow-ups.",
  "symptoms": "Between 03:15 and 03:40 UTC, multiple namespaces reported large numbers of Pending -> Evicted/Preempted events. Pod restart churn increased, user-reported 503s from inference endpoints, autoscaler oscillations triggered by rapid pod churn. Node available resources (Allocatable CPU/memory) did not show cluster-level shortage \u2014 rather, pods were being preempted out of nodes where they previously ran for days. Scheduler logs show increased Preemption decisions and score ties.",
  "quick_timeline": "2026-02-09 22:30 PST: rolling deploy of scheduler v1.27-custom with new scoring plugin (strict-topology) to control bin-packing\n2026-02-10 03:17 UTC: Pager triggered for increased pod restarts in us-west-2 prod cluster\n03:20 UTC: SRE oncall (Priya) starts triage, confirms spike in Preemption events via kubectl and Grafana\n03:28 UTC: Rolled back scheduler to previous version in control-plane for us-west-2 (partial)\n03:40 UTC: Preemption rate drops, evictions stabilize; follow-up investigation started",
  "metrics_observed": "Preemption rate: baseline ~0.05/hr -> spike peaking at ~32/hr across AZs;\nScheduler internal latency 99th: 120ms -> 650ms during spike;\nEviction count (pods): +560 in 30 minutes in production;\nNode pressure metrics (cpu/mem): no cluster-wide shortage, per-node CPU usage unchanged;\nPod startup time median: 2.1s -> 8.9s because of restart churn",
  "commands_run": "kubectl get events --all-namespaces --field-selector reason=Preempted -o wide | head -n 200\nkubectl describe node ip-10-0-4-23 | egrep -A4 'Non-terminated Pods'\njournalctl -u kube-scheduler -o cat | sed -n '1,200p' | grep -i preempt\nkubectl get pods -n prod -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,PRIORITY:.spec.priority,STATUS:.status.phase --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp | tail -n 100\ncurl -sS \"https://grafana.redwood.com/render/d-solo/cluster/scheduler-metrics?panelId=3&from=now-1h&to=now\" -o scheduler-preemption.png",
  "root_cause_hypotheses": "1) Scoring plugin change introduced different tie-breaking behavior that aggressively favors preempting medium-priority pods when topology-scores are tied.\n2) A scheduling race under load increased scheduler latency causing stale scheduling decisions and duplicate preemption candidates.\n3) Mistuned preemption cost heuristics in our custom scheduler fork (recent commit 4f3a9b) increased preemption score delta for low-memory nodes.\nEvidence: timing correlates with scheduler rollout; logs show many preemption decisions with identical scores; rollback reduced rate.",
  "mitigation_steps_taken": "1) Immediate rollback of scheduler binary in us-west-2 control plane partial rollout (~03:28 UTC).\n2) Temporarily increased eviction gracePeriod for critical namespaces to reduce restart churn (patch applied to pod disruption budgets).\n3) Added a temporary admission webhook block for best-effort pods in prod to avoid low-priority churn while we investigate.\nOutcome: preemption rate dropped to baseline within ~12 minutes of rollback; user-facing errors decreased.",
  "persistent_actions": "- Create a canary rollout plan for scheduler scoring plugin updates with traffic shaping and synthetic preemption checks.\n- Add unit/integration test that simulates score ties and verifies deterministic tie-breaking consistent with prior behavior.\n- Audit custom preemption heuristics in commit history and add guardrails (feature flag + kill switch).\n- Add Grafana alert to detect preemption rate > 5/hr sustained for 5 minutes per region.",
  "next_steps": "- Full postmortem to be written after deeper log correlation and scheduler trace capture (owner: Priya, due 2026-02-18).\n- Reproduce locally: create a mini-cluster with our custom scheduler and run the synthetic workload that caused tie scores. (Ethan)\n- Patch scheduler to preserve previous tie-break ordering or make tie-break explicit, then perform staged rollout with 1% canary. (Claire)\n- Follow up with product teams about autoscaler backoff behavior to reduce oscillation during similar events.",
  "notes_to_oncall": "If you see a preemption spike: 1) check scheduler rollout history (kubectl -n kube-system rollout history deployment/kube-scheduler); 2) query recent scheduler logs for 'Preemption' and 'score tie' strings; 3) consider partial rollback of scheduler binary if correlating with deploy; 4) temporarily raise critical pod terminationGracePeriod and pause non-essential jobs; 5) ping eng-sre Slack #sre-oncall and cc @Priya and @Ethan. Include timestamps and sample pod names when filing a follow-up Linear ticket.",
  "freeform_notes": "- Observed interesting pattern: many preempted pods shared same topologySpread constraints; scoring plugin was aggressively trying to satisfy topologies which produced more preemption candidates than before.\n- Autoscaler amplified problem: nodes freed by preemptions triggered scale-down observations in ASG, which then forced additional re-scheduling and further churn.\n- Consider adding a short cooldown on node-scale-down when preemption rate is high.\n- Need to coordinate rollback/playbook with Platform team to avoid control-plane config drift in future deploys.",
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "summary",
    "symptoms",
    "quick_timeline",
    "metrics_observed",
    "commands_run",
    "root_cause_hypotheses",
    "mitigation_steps_taken",
    "persistent_actions",
    "next_steps",
    "notes_to_oncall",
    "freeform_notes"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_62b9695b49a446acaa1f59a1427b8480"
}

arguments.content:
# Runtime Diagnostics — Operating Charter

Status: Approved team charter
Parent: Infrastructure & SRE
Executive sponsor and accountable leader: Rafael Mendes, Head of Site Reliability Engineering

## Mission

Reduce customer-impacting runtime incidents by turning cross-layer symptoms into reproducible diagnoses, validated mitigations, and safe release gates. Runtime Diagnostics is the directly responsible owner for the investigation lifecycle when a failure crosses runtime, scheduler, GPU fleet, cache, routing, or release boundaries.

## Owned failure modes

The team owns diagnostic leadership, evidence capture, reproduction, mitigation validation, and recurrence tracking for cold-start and warmup latency; KV-cache eviction, fragmentation, and rehydration storms; scheduler preemption and eviction waves; runtime OOMs and kernel or quantization regressions; midstream stalls and runtime-induced 5xx; release-correlated latency/error regressions; and runtime behavior during regional failover and restore.

## Boundaries and neighboring teams

- Serving Runtime owns product code, runtime architecture, and permanent component fixes. Runtime Diagnostics owns cross-layer isolation, reproducer quality, and acceptance evidence.
- Release Engineering owns pipelines and rollout execution. Runtime Diagnostics defines runtime health gates, supplies evidence, and may recommend pause/rollback; Release Engineering executes promotion or rollback.
- GPU Fleet/Platform owns capacity, nodes, networking, and control-plane changes. Runtime Diagnostics diagnoses runtime-facing effects and validates mitigations.
- Observability owns telemetry platforms. Runtime Diagnostics specifies missing signals and validates diagnostic usefulness.
- SRE on-call remains incident commander and availability owner. Runtime Diagnostics serves as specialist escalation and investigation DRI.
- Security approves sensitive access and artifact handling. Customer Support owns external communications.

## Intake and prioritization

Intake arrives through the incident bridge/on-call escalation or a tracked investigation ticket with timestamps, affected tier/region, release correlation, customer impact, dashboards/logs, and an accountable requester. P0/P1 active incidents preempt planned work; recurring P2s, failed release gates, failover anomalies, and ownership disputes enter weekly triage. The team acknowledges active-incident escalation immediately and assigns a named investigation DRI before leaving the bridge.

## Investigation, validation, and promotion

1. Preserve the timeline, release/config diffs, traces, profiles, logs, and affected cohort.
2. Form competing hypotheses and identify the smallest safe reproduction.
3. Correlate deployments in the preceding 60 minutes; quarantine suspect artifacts and pause promotion when warranted.
4. Reproduce in an isolated or staging environment and document negative evidence.
5. Validate the mitigation against baseline latency, errors, availability, eviction/preemption, and customer-tier constraints.
6. Promote staging → small canary → wider cohorts only with recorded approvals and an executable rollback.
7. Close only after monitoring confirms recovery, a permanent owner accepts follow-up work, and evidence is attached.

## Escalation

The incident commander retains command. Runtime Diagnostics escalates release risk to Release Engineering, capacity/control-plane risk to Platform or GPU Fleet, code defects to Serving Runtime, missing telemetry to Observability, and sensitive-data/access issues to Security. Any unresolved P0/P1 ownership dispute goes to Rafael Mendes; customer commitments or exception requests also require the responsible product and customer leaders.

## First-quarter goals

- Establish a baseline taxonomy and owner map for runtime incidents, including an explicit unknown/unowned queue.
- Publish diagnostic bundles and reproducible runbooks for the top recurring cold-start, cache-eviction, preemption, OOM/kernel, and streaming-stall signatures.
- Add runtime diagnostic checks to release canaries and exercise rollback with Release Engineering.
- Run a multi-region failover/restore diagnostic exercise with timestamped evidence.
- Reduce repeat incidents and time-to-diagnosis against the first-month baseline.
- Ramp Priya Shah to lead a scoped investigation under review and then independently.

## Evidence basis

- Incident themes show cold-start spikes correlated with nightly rollouts and unresolved ownership gaps: /knowledge/company/sources/slack/incidents/1890012345-themes-decomp-remediation-roundup.json (dsid_a450344da1bb43d79ceaf112861b5f4c).
- Recurring KV-cache evictions follow traffic spikes and shard hotness/TTL variability: /knowledge/company/sources/slack/incidents/1891023456-kv-cache-evictions-sync.json (dsid_d1eab7208aea4db0a3cfa8f197f19dbd).
- Failover incidents expose routing, delayed backups, and restore-runbook gaps: /knowledge/company/sources/slack/incidents/2255556789-dr-aftergame-assignments-and-radar.json (dsid_86f3cb6edffb487d889832a507515bf6).
- Runtime staffing was authorized and Priya’s offer approved with 30/60/90 milestones: /knowledge/company/sources/gmail/vanessa_ortiz/20270715-runtime-staffing-authorization-exec-summary.json (dsid_e4bf62d7247e4867b72c78eb1441d392).
